card: Applies scripted diffs across test and benchmark files to explicitly include util/check.h wherever assert or Assert is invoked, removing direct cassert includes and sorting modified include headers. This addresses ambiguity around whether assertions can be disabled by NDEBUG, clarifies assert versus Assert usage, and assists Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) tooling. The author observes that compiling without assertions in util/check.h causes build errors. The PR is marked draft while waiting on unspecified prerequisites.
evidence: PR description: 'In test code, `assert` is used. This is perfectly fine, but sometimes confusion arises, when it is unclear whether `NDEBUG` can disable the assertions, or whether to use `assert` or `Assert`.'
Commit 113fa13d90: 'The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions.'
problem: Test files rely on assertion macros without explicitly including `util/check.h`, creating ambiguity over whether assertions can be disabled by `NDEBUG` and whether `assert` or `Assert` should be used. The missing direct includes also complicate automated Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) tooling.

risk.why: Touches only header includes in test and benchmark files via mechanical verify scripts.

scope_notes: Mechanical scripted-diff touching include directives across 57 test files, followed by automated clang-format include sorting.
summary: Applies a scripted diff to add `#include <util/check.h>` across test and benchmark files that use `assert` or `Assert`, while removing redundant direct `<cassert>` includes. A second scripted commit sorts the modified include blocks using `clang-format-diff.py`.
